title: Greek
description: Everyday Greek in the Greek alphabet with romanization: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: 'Γεια σου' (ya sou) is hello and bye to one friend; 'γεια σας' (ya sas) is the polite or plural form.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: Greek uses 'the' with names and family words: 'η μητέρα μου' = the mother my (my mother).

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'Μου αρέσει' (mou aresei) means 'I like', literally 'it pleases me'.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: A Greek question mark looks like a semicolon: 'Πόσο κάνει;' = How much is it?

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: 'Πού' (pou) with an accent means where; 'που' without it means that/which.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: 'Το πρωί' (to proi) means in the morning and 'τη νύχτα' (ti nychta) at night.
